theme: Sports, Olympic & Paralympic Champions, Records, Experiences & Theatre

hero.title: Share Your Experiences
hero.subtitle: Discover remarkable world records, inspiring Paralympic achievements, swimming styles, hot-air balloon flights, and memorable stage performances.

stories.summary: Sofia and Nikos explore competitive swimming strokes, world records, and relay races at the Athens Aquatic Centre.
stories.narrative: Sofia and Nikos love swimming at the Olympic Aquatic Centre. Today they watch athletes compete in a big national competition. Swimmers race in four main styles: backstroke, breaststroke, butterfly, and fast freestyle. The crowd cheers when the reigning champion manages to beat the national record by two seconds. Sofia watches the official time board to compare the results. In the final event, the mixed relay team swims with power, and two swimmers touch the pool wall simultaneously. The winning athlete proudly lifts her gold medal as the new record holder.

stories.summary: The inspiring career of Konstantinos Fykas, double gold medalist at the Sydney Paralympics and world record holder.
stories.narrative: Konstantinos Fykas is an inspiring Greek athlete who achieved remarkable success at the Paralympics. When he was young, his teammates gave him the nickname Dolphin because of his exceptional speed in water. Daily swimming became a disciplined habit that helped him overcome severe physical challenges. In the Sydney games, he was able to dominate both the fifty metre and hundred metre races. His hard training helped him earn international praise. Fans compared his courage to the ancient runners of antiquity, and his gold medal figure stands as an unforgettable accomplishment and historic achievement in Greek sports history.

stories.summary: Alex boards a giant hot-air balloon across mountain valleys, spotting wildlife sanctuaries and festival crowds.
stories.narrative: Early in the morning, Alex and Maria prepare to board a giant hot-air balloon. The international contest was originally planned for yesterday, but clear skies today allow dozens of balloons to rise together among the misty hills. Floating silently high above, they witness the spectacular landscape stretching for miles. Alex uses his imagination to photograph the winding river below. They fly over a protected bird sanctuary where wild herons rest. A spectator on the grass holds a funny pet ferret on a lead. Near the landing destination, pupils deposit soda cans in a recycling bank while families enjoy roasted meat on a wooden skewer. More than one billion viewers around the world follow balloon racing festivals each year.

stories.summary: Elena and Giorgos attend a long-running musical in London and explore Greek theatre productions in Athens.
stories.narrative: Elena and Giorgos love theatrical entertainment. Last December in London, they attended a famous long-running musical in the West End. The talented actors captivate the packed audience with live songs and energetic dancing. The composer wrote magical melodies that were later adapted into a popular movie. Back in Athens, their school drama society decided to revive a classic Greek comedy by Aristophanes. The student production received an enthusiastic review in the local cultural newspaper. After the show, pupils enjoyed a lively post-show discussion with the director about stage lighting and costume design.

grammar_lab.title: Inductive Grammar Lab: Present Perfect & Experiences
grammar_lab.subtitle: Contrast Present Perfect Simple (life experiences) with Past Simple (definite times), and master Present Perfect Continuous with for and since.
target_structures: Present Perfect Simple: have/has + past participle (life experiences, results)
Past Simple: definite finished past time (in 2004, yesterday, when I was eight)
Present Perfect Continuous: have/has been + -ing (duration of ongoing actions)
Time expressions: ever, never, already, yet, for (duration), since (starting point)

rules.use: Talk about experiences in our life without mentioning a specific finished time.
examples: Have you ever flown in a hot-air balloon? — Yes, I have.
She has won three gold medals in swimming competitions.

rules.use: Use Present Perfect when the time is open/unspecified; switch to Past Simple as soon as a specific time is mentioned.
examples: I have visited London three times. (Life experience)
I went to London last summer and saw a musical. (Specific past time)

rules.structure: Present Perfect Continuous with FOR and SINCE
rules.use: Express actions that began in the past and are still continuing in the present.
examples: Konstantinos Fykas has been swimming since he was eight years old.
The actors have been rehearsing for three hours.

practice_items.prompt: ________ you ever flown in a colourful hot-air balloon?
options: Have
Did
Do
Are
practice_items.explanation: We use 'Have you ever + past participle' to ask about life experiences.

practice_items.prompt: Konstantinos Fykas ________ two gold medals at the Sydney Paralympics in 2000.
options: won
has won
was winning
wins
practice_items.explanation: A specific finished past time ('in 2000') requires the Past Simple.

practice_items.prompt: Elena has been acting in the school drama club ________ three years.
options: for
since
during
from
practice_items.explanation: 'For' indicates a period of duration ('three years').

practice_items.prompt: Nikos ________ competitive swimming since he was eight years old.
options: has been practicing
practiced
is practicing
practices
practice_items.explanation: An action starting in the past and continuing up to now with 'since' takes Present Perfect Continuous.

practice_items.prompt: The record-breaking swimmer has ________ touched the wall and won the race!
options: just
yet
ever
since
practice_items.explanation: 'Just' indicates an action completed a very short moment before the present.

school_lab_listening.title: Radio Programme: Interview with Champion Konstantinos Fykas
school_lab_listening.context: Listen to the radio presenter interview Greek Paralympic swimming champion Konstantinos Fykas about his achievements and training routine.

script_lines.speaker: Radio Host
script_lines.text: Good evening sports fans and welcome to Top Stories on the Radio. Tonight in our studio we have a true champion, Greek Paralympian swimmer Konstantinos Fykas. Welcome Konstantinos!

script_lines.speaker: Konstantinos
script_lines.text: Good evening! Thank you very much for inviting me to your show.

script_lines.speaker: Radio Host
script_lines.text: How long have you been swimming competitively, Konstantinos?

script_lines.speaker: Konstantinos
script_lines.text: I have been swimming since I was eight years old. Swimming became my daily habit and my passion.

script_lines.speaker: Radio Host
script_lines.text: You won two gold medals and set world records at the Sydney Paralympics. What is your advice for young pupils?

script_lines.speaker: Konstantinos
script_lines.text: Never give up on your dreams. With hard work, patience, and determination, you can accomplish anything in life.

writing_workshop.title: Class Book of Records: My Personal Best
writing_workshop.guidance: Write a report about an achievement, hobby record, or skill you have accomplished or practiced for a long time.

scaffold.opening: I have been [practicing/playing/studying] [activity] for [number] years / since [year/age].
scaffold.development: My biggest accomplishment so far was when I [what you did / competition you entered / challenge you beat].
scaffold.feelings: I felt very proud because I [worked hard / trained every week / never gave up].
scaffold.closing: In the future, I hope to [next goal or record you want to achieve].

can_do_checklist: I can name four different swimming styles (backstroke, breaststroke, butterfly, freestyle).
I can talk about my life experiences using the Present Perfect Simple (have you ever / I have never).
I can distinguish between Present Perfect (unspecified experience) and Past Simple (finished past time).
I can express duration of ongoing activities using Present Perfect Continuous with for and since.
I can write a report about an inspiring sports champion or my own personal record.
